title: Generate a tech pack with custom sizes
summary: Use your own size labels when you make a tech pack. We show how to enter them and choose your sample size.
body_markdown:
Click Custom before you generate. Choose who will wear the garment and the size system. Type your size labels with commas between them. Check the size tabs, choose your sample size, and click Generate Tech Pack.


[Watch on YouTube ↗](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BDk73dkeJLA)


## Before you start


- Know your size labels and which one you use for the sample.
- Have your garment ready to generate.


## How to do it


1.


### Choose Custom


Click Custom before you generate. Choose who will wear the garment. The example uses unisex.


2.


### Enter your size labels


Type the size headers with commas between them. The example uses 00, 0, 1, 2, and 3.


3.


### Check the tabs and sample size


Check that each label has its own size tab. Choose your sample size and edit any headers you need to change.


4.


### Start your tech pack


Click Generate Tech Pack. When it finishes, check the size labels and measurements.


## An example


### Sizes 00 to 3


Enter 00, 0, 1, 2, 3 as separate labels. Keep 00 and 0 as two different sizes. Then choose your sample size.


## Things to check


- Put a comma between each size label so it gets its own tab.
- Keep 00 and 0 as two different labels. Do not turn the labels into numbers.
- Check your sample size before you generate. Your team still needs to check fit and grading.


## A few common questions


Can I use sizes other than S, M and L?


Yes. Click Custom and type your labels with commas between them. The example uses 00, 0, 1, 2, and 3.


How do I check my custom sizes?


Each label should have its own tab. Check the labels and change any headers before you generate.


When do I choose the sample size?


Choose it when you set up your size range, before you click Generate Tech Pack.


## Video transcript


Read the transcript


Now I’m going to show you how to generate a tech pack with your own size range. Before you generate, choose the sizes you need. You can write your own custom sizing. Click Custom, then choose who will wear this garment. We’ll keep it as unisex. I can change the size system. For example, I can use 00, 0, 1, 2, and 3 and enter all of that here. Then I can choose my sample size. Type in the headers for the measurement sizes you want to use. Use commas to separate the size headers. You’ll see little tabs appear when it works. You can edit them here too. This is how you build a custom size system. When you’re done, click Generate Tech Pack.
